feature.title: Creating a Promotion
feature.contentMd:
## What It Does
Allows a trade marketing team or integration system to define a new promotional offer. A promotion specifies the discount type, which products and outlets it applies to, the validity period, and any spending or usage limits.

Promotions can be created one at a time through the Promo Management UI, or uploaded in bulk via MDM or system integration.

## Common Questions
- **How do I create a new promotion?** Use the Promo Management UI in DMS to fill in promo details, or upload in bulk via MDM/integration.
- **Can I upload multiple promotions at once?** Yes — use batch upload via MDM or integration API.
- **Can I pause a promotion without deleting it?** Yes — deactivate it. You can reactivate it later.
- **What information is needed to create a promo?** At minimum: promo ID, promo type (discount or free goods), start date, and end date.
- **Is there a draft or approval workflow?** Currently, no — promotions go live immediately on submission.

## Scope
### In Scope
- Single promo creation via UI
- Batch promo upload via MDM/integration
- Activation and deactivation of promos
- Updating promo validity dates
- Audit logging of promo creation

### Out of Scope
- Draft/save-and-edit workflow (not supported currently)
- Approval flow before going live

## Who Uses It
- **Trade Marketing Manager** — creates and configures promotions via the Promo Management UI in DMS
- **MDM / Integration System** — pushes promotions in bulk via API
- **Regional Sales Manager** — reviews promotions for their area

## Rules
1. Every promotion must have a promo ID, promo type, start date, and end date
2. A promotion can be created individually or as part of a batch upload
3. When a promo is created, the system automatically sets up outlet targeting, location targeting, product assignments, and budget tracking
4. Promotions can be activated or deactivated without deletion
5. Every promo creation is audit-logged with the creator identity

## Data & Fields
| Field | Description | Required | Example |
|-------|-------------|----------|--------|
| Promo ID | Unique identifier for the promotion | Yes | PROMO-2024-SUMMER-001 |
| Promo Title | Human-readable name | No | Summer Push 10% |
| Promo Type | Category of promotion | Yes | Discount / FOC |
| Start Date | When the promo becomes active | Yes | 2024-06-01 |
| End Date | When the promo expires | Yes | 2024-08-31 |
| Active Periods | Recurring validity windows | No | Weekends only |
| Source | Origin of the promo | No | UI / MDM / Integration |
| Created By | User who created the promo | Yes | john.doe@company.com |

## Tenant-Level Configurations
| Config Point | Options | Default | Example |
|-------------|---------|---------|--------|
| Outlet targeting setup | Maps attributes to targeting criteria | Tenant-specific | OutletType, Channel, Segment |
| Location targeting setup | Configures location-based targeting attributes | Tenant-specific | Region, Territory, Area |
| Custom field mapping | Controls how custom fields are mapped | Tenant-specific | Field mapping per entity |

## Open Questions
- [ ] promoGroupId — exact conflict resolution behavior (client-specific)
- [ ] applicationType — possible values and meaning

scenarios.title: Creating a Promotion via UI
scenarios.contentMd:
## User Flow
1. Trade marketing manager opens the Promo Management UI in DMS
2. Selects the promo type (Discount or Free Goods)
3. Fills in basic details: Promo title, start date, end date
4. Selects the eligibility rule — how products or orders qualify (e.g., per item, invoice total, product group)
5. Selects the discount method — what benefit is given (e.g., percentage off, flat discount, free goods)
6. Defines slab structure with ranges and benefits (e.g., buy 10-20 cases → 5% off, 21-50 → 10%)
7. Sets outlet targeting criteria (outlet type, channel, key account, etc.)
8. Sets location targeting (region, territory, area)
9. Selects product scope — which products qualify for the promo
10. Optionally adds must-buy products — products that MUST be in the order
11. Sets budget limits (total spending cap in ₹ or quantity)
12. Sets usage limits (max number of times the promo can be used)
13. Submits the promotion — it goes live immediately

## Example
A trade marketing manager wants to run a summer promotion:
- **Promo**: 'Summer Beverage Push' — 10% off on beverages
- **Dates**: June 1 to August 31
- **Outlets**: Gold-tier outlets in Modern Trade channel
- **Products**: All Beverages category
- **Budget**: ₹5,00,000 total
- **Usage limit**: Max 1,000 orders

They fill these details in the UI, submit, and the promo goes live for eligible outlets immediately.

## Rules
1. All required fields must be filled: promo ID, type, start date, end date
2. Outlet targeting criteria are validated before saving
3. No draft mode — promo goes live on submission
4. The system sets up all promotion components automatically: definition, outlet targeting, location targeting, product assignments, and budget tracking
5. Every creation is audit-logged with the user identity and timestamp

scenarios.title: Batch Promo Upload via MDM/Integration
scenarios.contentMd:
## User Flow
1. MDM system or integration partner prepares a batch of promo definitions in the expected format
2. Sends the batch via the API endpoint
3. System processes each promo individually within the batch
4. Valid promotions are created and immediately active
5. Invalid promotions are rejected with error details

## Example
A company wants to upload 50 regional promotions at once:
- The MDM team prepares a file with 50 promo definitions, each with different regional targeting
- They send the batch to the API
- 48 promotions pass validation and go live
- 2 promotions are rejected because of missing required fields (start date)
- The team fixes the 2 rejected promos and re-uploads them

## Rules
1. Each promo in the batch is processed independently — one failure does not block others
2. Each promo is prepared with the necessary configuration before processing
3. Audit log records the batch source and individual promo IDs
4. Same validation rules apply as UI creation
5. Batch upload is commonly used by large companies managing hundreds of promotions per quarter

scenarios.title: Activating and Deactivating Promotions
scenarios.contentMd:
## User Flow
1. User navigates to the promo list in the Promo Management UI
2. Finds the target promotion by searching or filtering
3. Toggles the active/inactive status
4. Changes take effect for new orders immediately

## Example
A summer promotion is running but the company has exceeded its quarterly budget:
- Trade marketing manager opens Promo Management UI
- Finds 'Summer Beverage Push' promotion
- Clicks deactivate → promo is now inactive
- New orders placed after this will NOT receive the discount
- Existing orders that already had the discount applied are NOT affected
- Later, when budget is replenished, the manager re-activates the promo

## Rules
1. Deactivating a promo stops it from being applied to new orders
2. Already-applied discounts on existing orders are NOT affected — they stay as-is
3. Promo validity dates can be updated even after creation
4. Activation/deactivation is audit-logged with who made the change and when
5. There is no time limit on deactivation — a promo can be deactivated and reactivated at any time
